comment: Review findings. Four independent reviews of codex/ui-audit-pass, each
given the spec and the diff and never another reviewer's reasoning.
verdict is provenance, not severity. 'reported' means a reviewer claimed
it and nobody has re-derived it here yet — a claim from a delegated agent
is a lead. 'confirmed' means it was reproduced in this repo, and the
evidence field carries the numbers or the code read that did it.
falsified is 1 only when the guard was made to FAIL against the restored
defect. A fix with falsified 0 is a fix nobody has proved is load-bearing.
The two earlier reviews (browser, lib) are recorded at the granularity
that survived the session; their per-finding detail is in the transcript,
not here. Findings raised after this file existed are recorded whole.

findings.claim: Damage facts are built from @smogon/calc's fixed 3-hit pin while the engine rolls 2-5, so min/max/critMax/possibleKO/guaranteedKO all describe a move the game does not play.
findings.evidence: Probed: Icicle Spear, Rock Blast, Bullet Seed, Tail Slap all report calc .hits === 3. Cloyster Icicle Spear vs 250 HP Blissey read max=198 critMax=297 possibleKO=false; five hits deal 330 and five crits 495. Against 160 HP it read guaranteedKO=true, which two max-roll hits miss 35% of the time. After the fix: max=330 critMax=495 possibleKO=true, guaranteedKO=false.

findings.claim: Slush Rush is given hail immunity it does not have in Gen 8, so a hail attrition line predicts zero chip per turn where the game deals 1/16.
findings.evidence: Read the block directly. Root cause was ours: docs/CONSTANTS-AUDIT.md D11 read 'Ice Body/Snow Cloak/Slush Rush take no hail chip'. Hail is not symmetric with sand — sand exempts all three of its abilities, hail exempts only Ice Body and Snow Cloak. This repo's own ai/src/abilities.ts and ai/src/order.ts only ever gave Slush Rush a speed effect. Audit entry corrected rather than silently edited.

findings.claim: There are two disjoint representations of 'this was a crit'. A sampled crit sets criticalHitTargets but never fires Anger Point; a guaranteed crit fires Anger Point but never appears in the log.
findings.evidence: Probed. Machamp Tackle vs Anger Point Tauros, crit sampled: criticalHitTargets=["player-1"], boosts=undefined. Storm Throw (always-crit): criticalHitTargets=undefined, boosts={"player-1":{"atk":6}}. The 1/16 event Anger Point exists for cannot trigger it. Fixed in 0ff6e6a. Both paths now record into criticalHitTargets and Anger Point reads the resolved answer per target, so a spread move can crit one side only. The facts stay as a fallback for callers that supply damage directly instead of sampling.

findings.claim: criticalByTarget is one boolean per target, so a single crit draw applies to every hit of a multi-hit move. Mainline rolls the crit per hit.
findings.evidence: Probed Rock Blast: crit forced gives all hits identical, no-crit gives all hits identical — never mixed. Real 5-hit P(at least one crit) is 27.6% spread across 1-5 crit hits; this engine gives 6.25% all-five and 93.75% none. The mean survives, the distribution does not. Fixed in 0ff6e6a. Measured after: 30.1% of five-hit Rock Blasts crit over 627 samples against a theoretical 27.6% (1.4 standard errors), with zero all-five crits. The test classifies hits by damage band — ordinary 37-44, crit 56-66, disjoint — because an earlier version counted distinct damage values, which vary from ordinary roll spread regardless, and stayed green when hit 0's flag was applied to all five.

findings.claim: Moving the sleep counter onto the attempt made statusTurns === 0 unreachable, but three legality gates still test it, so Sleep Talk and Snore execute on the turn the user wakes.
findings.evidence: Probed at statusTurns=1. Sleep Talk: hit=true, notes 'actor woke on the attempt and acted' then 'Sleep Talk selected Tackle'. Snore: 19 damage. Mainline wakes the Pokemon and it does nothing. Gates at move-engine.ts:3106, actions.ts:594, call-legality.ts:42. Fixed in 16f664c. The rule now lives in ai/src/sleep.ts so the three gates cannot drift apart again. An undefined counter still counts as asleep, matching the old behaviour, rather than inventing a wake for hand-built states.

findings.claim: The held-item flinch never calls blocksSecondaryEffects and gates on total damage rather than direct damage, so it flinches through Shield Dust and through a Substitute.
findings.evidence: Probed Machamp + King's Rock Tackle at roll 0.05: flinch applied vs Shield Dust, vs Substitute, and vs the bare control alike. The move's OWN flinch secondary is correctly blocked in both cases, so only the item path is wrong. sequentialDamageOutcome(...).directDamage is computed 20 lines below and is the value it should gate on. Fixed in 16f664c by reusing effectTargetIds — the set the engine already computes for who receives a move's added effects, and where the Substitute filter lives (move-engine.ts:3528). canApplyVolatile does NOT check Substitute or Shield Dust; probed directly, it returns true for both. Shield Dust comes from blocksSecondaryEffects, the same call the secondary path makes.

findings.claim: The diff cites onBeforeMovePriority to move confusion above paralysis but leaves paralysis above infatuation, which the same ordering forbids. Reported marginals: mainline 33.0/33.5/8.4, this engine 33.0/25.1/16.75.
Showdown's Rainbow condition explicitly skips the doubling for a Serene Grace flinch secondary, so the x4 is wrong for the exact example the comment cites. 60% is correct there.

On the hitRolls branch pickRoll is called without the critical argument, so a rolled crit never reaches the damage — but criticalHitTargets and the trace note are set anyway. The announced crit deals less than the ordinary hit.
critBlocked checks the defender's ability but never calls ignoresTargetAbility, so a Mold Breaker attacker never crits a Battle Armor or Shell Armor target.

The mechanics wave added three draw sites, removed one and reordered two, but seed-keyed receipts record only schemaVersion. Every receipt written before the change now replays to different outcomes with no signal.
findings.evidence: Widened by 0ff6e6a: a variable multi-hit now draws N crits instead of 1, so seeded replay of any multi-hit move diverges from receipts written before it. Still only schemaVersion is checked.

findings.claim: Mainline runs sleep above truant and flinch, so the counter burns even on a flinched turn. Here both return first, so a flinched sleeper sleeps one turn longer. The recharge case is correct.

getEffectiveMoveMetadata returns defaults.multiHitRange unconditionally, and resolution puts hitCountOverride ahead of targetFacts.hits, so an explicit MoveState hits is honoured by the calculator then overwritten. Not currently reachable.
status.ts keeps a second crit list that folds in the always-crit four, so the Focus Energy policy believes it helps a Wicked Blow. Two hand-maintained copies of the same list is a drift hazard.
decrementSleep is now a no-op shim. Either the bookkeeping its comment mentions is real and should be named, or the function and its call site should go.

assert.equal(entry.chance, recomputed && entry.chance) evaluates to entry.chance whenever the recomputed value is non-zero, so the assertion compares a value to itself and the recomputed number is discarded.
findings.evidence: Read the source. Auditor also shifted the real quote by -5% and by hardcoding the catch rate to 255, both green. The fixture is Poochyena, whose rate IS 255, so the test cannot tell 'reads the rate' from 'hardcodes it' — and the test hardcodes it too.

findings.claim: The test's own 'the race was actually staged' assertion only proves a DOM button exists. Making a move click send no request at all — race physically impossible — still passes. Either guard can also be deleted alone and it stays green.
findings.evidence: Auditor's mutation: guard the move click with an early return so no /run/battle/act request is issued. 1/1 pass. Fix is to count requests through page.route rather than assert a node exists.

findings.claim: The test claims the suspect-clock flag is part of the hash chain from birth, but deleting it from eventHashInput keeps the test green, because the hash is computed the same wrong way at write and at validate.
findings.evidence: Read eventHashInput: it deletes only id and eventHash, so production IS correct and the flag is covered. This is a test gap, not a production bug. Closing it means tampering with a bundle and expecting CORRUPT_EVENT.

findings.claim: The shelf test only ever passes the correct prior checksum, so weakening the guard to accept any truthy supersedes stays green. A caller shipping supersedes: 'x' would overwrite any archive.
findings.evidence: Read the guard: production correctly requires incoming.supersedes === priorMark. Test gap. Closing it means asserting a wrong checksum is rejected with ARCHIVE_CONFLICT.

findings.claim: The test's comment says it pins the outspeed-KO exemption, but every cell in the fixture short-circuits before that branch, so deleting the exemption entirely keeps it green.
findings.evidence: Found independently before the audit returned. Measured on the fixture: every pairing has critKO=false, so the outspeed branch is never evaluated. Closed by testing pairingLethal directly as an exported function; that unit test goes red when the credit is removed.

findings.claim: answer.steps is empty for the fixture, so the forEach over it runs zero assertions. Unwiring the shared-bag ledger completely left 82/82 green.
findings.evidence: Fourth vacuous test found this session. Closed by extracting affordableOptions() and pinning the selection rule directly; restoring the unfunded fallback turns it red. The end-to-end count was left out on purpose and the test says so.

findings.claim: The focus-ring assertion is substring presence in a CSS file, so keeping the selector and deleting its outline declaration stays green. Sibling assertions on the same line use a real regex and do bite.

The fix left both hand-rolled crit lists in place and the test reaches only the calc-adapter copy, so the original defect can be reintroduced in status.ts and stay green. Sky Attack and Snipe Shot are named in a comment but asserted nowhere.
The Math.random guard covers only the ordinary-move advanceTurn call. Removing the rng from the forced-replacement site or the ball-throw site leaves the test green, and the fix repaired all three.
27 of 28 tests in the file carry a skip guard; the one added by this diff does not, so without Chromium it throws instead of skipping and breaks the file's stated contract.
When nothing affordable improved a Pokemon the selection fell back to the unfunded list, so one Focus Sash could be handed to three Pokemon and each was told it was now safe.
findings.evidence: Could not reproduce the reviewer's exact repro with a 3-mon party, but the rule was unsound on reading and pickups are never in the bag by construction, so affordableFromBag returns false for every pickup option. Fixed by removing the fallback outright.

findings.claim: pairingLethal credits 'we outspeed and KO on our worst roll' without checking whether their crit comes from a priority move. Mach Punch swings first no matter how fast we are.
findings.evidence: Priority moves appear in real exposure lists. Cells now carry critPriority from lib/planner.js and the credit is refused when set. The test goes red when critPriority is ignored.

findings.claim: archive() never named what it replaced and list() aborted the whole legacy import on the first conflict, despite an earlier commit message claiming both were wired.
findings.evidence: The edit was claimed in a commit message and was not in the file. Now wired, with legacy records imported one at a time so one conflict cannot lose the rest.

findings.claim: normalizeArchive stamped archivedAt from the wall clock, so the same run hashed differently on every archive and no content-addressed comparison could hold.
findings.evidence: archivedAt now derives from endedAt or startedAt, or is null.

findings.claim: 47 authored :hover rules were unguarded, so on a touch screen a tapped button keeps its hover background and reads as still-selected. The app is responsive to 640px and is held while playing.
findings.evidence: Counted through the CSSOM in a real browser, not by grepping source. Before: 35 bare hover rules live at 375x812 with pointer:coarse. After: 47 inert, 0 focus-visible trapped behind the guard, 30 remaining are vendor (bootstrap 28, select2 2) and deliberately out of scope. Desktop hover still works: border rgb(46,58,68) -> rgb(74,90,102).

findings.claim: The first pass of the hover codemod scoped itself to two stylesheets by assumption, so dark-theme.css kept 5 unguarded :hover rules while the new source gate reported green.
findings.evidence: Only a CSSOM count in a running browser found it — the source-level gate could not, because the gate and the codemod shared the same wrong file list. Worth remembering: a gate that reads the same scope as the fix cannot check the scope.

findings.claim: Nothing asserts that per-commit cost stays flat as the log grows. The wall-clock assertion that used to stand there was removed because it measured machine load, and no contention-proof replacement was found.
findings.evidence: Original gate: 11.5s under the full suite, 2.5s alone, identical code. A scaling ratio (second 5000 commits over the first) was tried and is also load-sensitive: 0.83-0.94 alone, 2.43 in suite. The loop IS flat — per-1000 blocks measured 88, 94, 67, 57, 49, 54, 65, 55, 61 ms — and an injected O(n) scan does show up at 2.57, but the healthy and loaded ranges overlap so the gate cannot separate them. Needs either a serialized perf lane or an operation counter rather than a clock.
